title: Coevolution of Life and Earth
seo_title: Coevolution of Life and Earth Worksheets: Oxygen, Ozone and Mass Extinctions (Earth Science)
standard_text: Construct an argument based on evidence about the simultaneous coevolution of Earth's systems and life on Earth.
meta_desc: Free high school Earth and space science worksheets on the coevolution of life and Earth (NGSS HS-ESS2-7): oxygen from cyanobacteria, banded iron, ozone, soils, extinctions and the timeline of life. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Life and Earth change each other.
key_sub: Microbes made oxygen; oxygen, ozone and impacts then shaped what could live.
body_html:
How to think about it

Life and Earth have changed each other for billions of years.

  • Life → Earth: cyanobacteria made oxygen (banded iron, ozone layer); plants made soil and coal; corals made limestone.
  • Earth → life: oxygen and ozone allowed animals and land life; impacts, eruptions, ice ages and drifting continents drove extinctions and new species.
  • Arguments use evidence from rocks, fossils and the timing of events.
Example

Banded iron formations appear ~2.4 billion years ago. What do they show?

Iron rusted out of seawater

Answer: oxygen was building up

Example

Land plants spread. Effect on CO₂?

More weathering and buried carbon

Answer: CO₂ fell

Common mistakes

  • Thinking Earth always had oxygen.
  • Thinking life only adapts and never changes Earth.
  • Thinking animals made the first oxygen.

faq.q: What does coevolution of life and Earth mean?
faq.a: Living things change Earth's air, water and rocks, and those changes in turn affect which living things can survive and evolve.

faq.q: Where did Earth's oxygen come from?
faq.a: From photosynthesis, first by cyanobacteria in the oceans starting about 2.7 billion years ago, and later by algae and plants.

faq.q: How did the ozone layer help life?
faq.a: Ozone formed from oxygen and blocks harmful ultraviolet light, which made it possible for plants and animals to live on land.
